chunks: He who thinks that God will not help him in this world and the next should stretch a rope to the sky then cut it off and see if his mind is relieved (of doubts) by this stratagem.
ai.seo_question: What does the metaphor of stretching a rope to the sky mean in Surah Al-Hajj?
ai.summary: In Shia exegesis, this verse is often interpreted as addressing the hypocrites or those whose doubt in divine support leads to self-sabotage, where their own 'stratagem' (kayd) becomes the cause of their ruin. The metaphor of stretching a rope to the sky signifies reaching for a solution that is ultimately futile, emphasizing that God's help is certain for the believers in both the worldly and hereafter realms. This highlights the practical implication that persistent doubt manifests as a spiritual disconnect, causing one's own efforts to fail in alleviating their inner turmoil.
